phase3_findings.description: test_tool_dialect_alone_decides_the_output is parametrized only [None, "sqlite"]; its SQLite outcome differs under mysql only because sqlglot's MySQL grammar reads # as a comment, and criterion 6 then requires a mysql case in the same test with the same meaning in MySQL syntax asserting the SQLite outcome, which the test lacks.

test_hash_is_not_a_comment_outside_mysql has only a sqlite case (is_introspection_query("#x\nSHOW 'abc", dialect="sqlite") is False); criterion 6 requires a mysql case in the same test with the same meaning in MySQL syntax asserting False, and the mysql row of test_untokenizable_show_is_data is a different test.

_CatalogCursor.execute picks the catalog query it answers from the parameter shape, so a two-name routine lookup whose second name is a kinds key, or a relation missing from kinds while named in routines, gets the wrong answer; FakeMySQL.rows is normalized to a list only at construction, so a later non-sequence assignment makes the fake raise TypeError.

The comment says a test whose fake connect was missed fails the same way on every machine, but a real connect to db.invalid depends on the resolver; test_validate_check_db_reports_failure (lines 320-328) never asserts mysql_connect was called, so it could pass after a real connect. The same claim was fixed in tests/integration/conftest.py but not here.

In test_rls_query_shapes_return_scoped_rows the finally block runs two DROP TABLE IF EXISTS calls in a row; if the first raises, the second table stays on the shared server and the cleanup error hides the original failure (same shape at line 141).
